article.title: What comes after Riyadh meeting between the Pakistani, Saudi and Turkish military chiefs?
article.summary: The hurriedmeetingof the military chiefs of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in Riyadh on Friday, followed by a separate meeting between Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman points to how quickly theMakkah Joint Defence Agreementis transitioning to an operational phase.The statements issued after the two meetings do not contain anything that would suggest that joint strikes or ground operations against Yemen’s Ansar Allah — commonly referred to as Houthis — are in the offing. However, the two communiques do show that the agreement signed on August 7 in Makkah is shifting gears from political assurances to putting in place the military arrangements required to give practical effect to its collective defence commitment.That is one notable change since the signing of the agreement. article.title: Military chiefs of Turkiye, Pakistan, KSA hold talks
article.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye have reaffirmed their commitment to collective defence, pledging to immediately translate the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement into effective military cooperation amid growing security threats to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.The commitment was made during a high-level meeting of the Chiefs of Defence Forces and Chiefs of General Staff of the three countries in Riyadh on Friday, September 25, according to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) on Saturday.The military leadership strongly condemned the attacks targeting the Holy City of Makkah and Saudi Arabia’s civilian and economic infrastructure, while reaffirming their determination to defend the Kingdom’s security, sovereignty and territorial integrity.The participants reviewed the evolving security situation and threats facing Saudi Arabia and appreciated the vigilance and professionalism of the Saudi Armed Forces in ensuring the safety of the population and th...

article.title: Saudi coalition says it intercepts Houthi missiles, drones
article.summary: CAIRO: Yemen’s Saudi-led coalition said early on Saturday it had intercepted two ballistic missiles and two drones launched by the Houthis towards the kingdom.The coalition said in posts on X that the missiles were headed towards Khamis Mushait and the drones towards the capital, Riyadh, adding that it was monitoring the missile threat and drones launched at the kingdom, without providing further details.The Saudi civil defence had sent alerts overnight for Khamis Mushait and Abha but not for Riyadh.The Houthis, who control the most populous parts of Yemen and much of the north, have been launching attacks against Saudi Arabia since declaring a naval blockade against Riyadh in July, with strikes targeting Saudi vessels in the Red Sea.Saudi Arabia thwarts Houthi ballistic missiles, Yemen’s Saudi-led coalition saysThe attacks have targeted Saudi cities, energy infrastructure and shipping, adding to pressures on global oil supplies caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran and putting at ri...

article.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye mull meeting of military chiefs to assist Riyadh under Makkah defence pact: FO
article.summary: The foreign ministers of Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia discussed plans on Friday to convene a meeting of the three countries’ chiefs of staff to explore ways to assist Riyadh under the Makkah Defence Alliance, according to the Foreign Office (FO).The FO statement noted that the tripartite agreement,signedon Aug 7, stipulated that an attack against any one of its parties should be considered an attack against all parties.Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar from Pakistan, Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan bin Abdullah and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan held a discussion on the defence pact on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.Earlier, Saudi Foreign Ministry alsoposted on Xthat the three member states condemned the recent Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia and discussed arrangements to convene an “urgent meeting of the chiefs of staff of the three countries” to support the Gulf state within the pact....

article.title: Pakistani, Saudi, Turkish chiefs discuss closer military ties
article.summary: Sept 26 (Reuters) - The military chiefs of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey discussed enhancing intelligence sharing, military coordination and capability integration at a meeting in Riyadh on Friday, according to statements from Saudi Arabia's Defence Ministry and Pakistan's military.The chiefs of defence forces and chiefs of general staff reviewed the security situation and threats facing Saudi Arabia and condemned attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis targeting the holy city of Makkah as well as the kingdom's civilian and economic infrastructure, the statements said.

article.title: UN Security Council condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
article.summary: UN Security Council condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi ArabiaThe United Nations Security Council on Friday condemned escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Houthis in a rare show of unity from the UN's top body.The Houthis have imposed a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, hitting its tankers, seizing swathes of Yemen's Red Sea coast vital for oil exports and causing energy prices to jump, while also raining missiles on the kingdom."The members of the Security Council condemned, in the strongest terms, continued Houthi attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including attacks impacting civilian and energy infrastructure, which have resulted in the injury of civilians, including women and children," said the rotating president of the Council, French UN envoy Jerome Bonnafont, delivering a joint statement.
